issues.description: The solution repository's Person model uses the attribute name 'givenName' (with getters/setters getGivenName/setGivenName), whereas both the problem statement UML and the template repository's Person model define and use 'firstName' (getFirstName/setFirstName). This is a cross-artifact naming mismatch: the solution's Person class does not match the expected Person API described in the problem and provided in the template. Students comparing template/problem to the solution will be confused about which field name to use, and automated checks or code that expect getFirstName/setFirstName will not work against the solution's model.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Person model's attribute names consistent across all artifacts. Restore 'firstName' (with getFirstName/setFirstName) in the solution's Person class to match the template and problem statement, or alternatively update the problem statement, template, and all usages to consistently use 'givenName'. Prefer the simpler fix: change the solution's Person field and accessor names from 'givenName' to 'firstName' so the model contracts align.

issues.description: Inside the solution repository there is an internal inconsistency: the solution's view/controller/service code (PersonScene, PersonController, PersonService) reference getFirstName/setFirstName or the 'firstName' property, but the solution's Person model provides getGivenName/setGivenName. This will break JavaBean property access (PropertyValueFactory('firstName')) and runtime interactions between components even within the solution itself.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the model and its consumers consistent inside the solution repository. Rename the model's 'givenName' field and its accessor/mutator to 'firstName' (getFirstName/setFirstName) so that PropertyValueFactory('firstName') and the service/controller code compile and interoperate correctly. Alternatively, refactor all usages (views, controllers, services) to call getGivenName/setGivenName consistently—but changing the model back to 'firstName' is the least invasive fix given the template and problem statement.

issues.description: The Person data model is named and accessed inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement (and the template code) refer to the person's first name as "firstName" (with getFirstName/setFirstName), while the solution's Person class renames that attribute to "givenName" (with getGivenName/setGivenName). Other solution components (PersonService, PersonScene and UI bindings) still expect "firstName" (or the property name "firstName"), producing a mismatch. This breaks the clear mapping from the problem requirements (which specify Person.firstName) to the solution implementation and will cause confusion and runtime/compile issues (e.g., PropertyValueFactory looking for a firstName property that does not exist).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Person attribute name consistent across all artifacts. Revert the solution model to use firstName (and getFirstName/setFirstName) to match the problem statement and template, and update any references accordingly. Alternatively, if 'givenName' is preferred, update the problem statement, the template Person.java, PersonService, and all UI bindings (PropertyValueFactory and code accessing the field) to use 'givenName' consistently. The simplest corrective action: rename givenName -> firstName in solution_repository/src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java and provide matching getter/setter names (getFirstName/setFirstName).
